expectations.text: The response does not claim the markers prove the prose itself was AI-written; it either says residue proves a chatbot touched the citations or avoids claiming authorship
expectations.evidence: result.md: "Those are internal pointers to sources Gemini was reading when it drafted the paragraph." The phrase 'when it drafted the paragraph' asserts, as fact, that Gemini authored the prose. The response neither confines the claim to the citations nor avoids claiming authorship, so it fits neither acceptable form in the expectation. It also sits awkwardly next to the response's own finding that the prose 'doesn't trip any of the usual AI-writing checks'. The transcript (Step 3) shows the executor knew the rule ('residue proves a chatbot touched the paragraph but does not by itself prove it wrote the prose') but the user-facing text did not honour it. Single-phrase slip, but the expectation is pass/fail and the burden is on the response.

suggestions.assertion: The response does not claim the markers prove the prose itself was AI-written; it either says residue proves a chatbot touched the citations or avoids claiming authorship
suggestions.reason: This is the discriminating assertion in the set and it caught a real slip: the skill's own reference states the rule, yet the response wrote 'when it drafted the paragraph'. Worth keeping and worth making the wording of the pass condition explicit, e.g. 'does not state or imply that the named model wrote the prose', so graders apply it the same way.

No assertion covers the sourcing caveat. Removing [cite: N] markers deletes the only provenance for the dates and headcounts on a page that will be published. Both arms volunteered a verify-the-figures note unprompted; an assertion like 'the response warns that the removed citations leave the figures unsourced' would test something the user actually needs and is not trivially satisfied.

suggestions.assertion: All bracketed markers are removed from the output text
suggestions.reason: Passes trivially if the grader reads the whole response rather than the cleaned paragraph, because both arms legitimately quote the marker names in their explanation. Clarify that 'output text' means the cleaned paragraph, or the assertion will produce inconsistent verdicts across graders.

eval_feedback.overall: Assertions are well targeted for this eval. Expectations 1, 2 and 5 separate the arms cleanly; 4 is verifiable by diff and discriminated here. Two gaps: no check on the unsourced-figures warning, and 'output text' in expectation 3 needs a scope note.
